facts.value: Overtime at 1.5x is owed after 40 hours/week, OR more than 12 hours/day, OR 12 consecutive hours (whichever yields the most pay).
facts.summary: Unlike federal law, Colorado requires daily overtime after 12 hours in a workday or 12 consecutive hours, in addition to the 40-hour weekly threshold.
facts.sourceAgency: Colorado Dept of Labor & Employment, Division of Labor Standards and Statistics
facts.notes: COMPS Order is updated annually; confirm current order number for 2026.

facts.summary: Colorado's 2026 salary threshold for the executive/administrative/professional (EAP) overtime exemption is higher than the federal $684/week floor.
facts.sourceAgency: Colorado Dept of Labor & Employment, Division of Labor Standards and Statistics
facts.notes: Highly compensated employee threshold for 2026 is $130,014/yr (2.25x EAP). Source is CDLE INFO #1 summary of the adopted 2026 PAY CALC Order; verify weekly figure against the PAY CALC Order text.

facts.summary: Colorado's statewide minimum wage is $15.16/hour effective January 1, 2026, well above the federal $7.25; some localities (e.g., Denver) set higher rates.
facts.citation: Colo. Const. art. XVIII, sec. 15; 7 CCR 1103-1 (COMPS Order)
facts.sourceAgency: Colorado Dept of Labor & Employment, Division of Labor Standards and Statistics
facts.notes: Adjusted annually for CPI. Tipped minimum is $3.02 less. Local minimum wages may be higher (see CDLE INFO #19).

facts.summary: The Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act protects several classes beyond the federal set, including sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, marital status, ancestry, and creed.
facts.notes: List reflects CCRD's stated protected classes plus the federally-covered base classes (race, color, religion, national origin, sex, disability, age); verify exact statutory enumeration in C.R.S. 24-34-402.

facts.value: 1 or more employees (no minimum size threshold)
facts.summary: CADA covers essentially all Colorado employers regardless of size, far broader than the federal 15-employee threshold under Title VII/ADA.
facts.notes: CCRD states any employee working in Colorado is covered; certain religious organizations are excluded. Verify statutory 'employer' definition at C.R.S. 24-34-401(3).

facts.summary: A Colorado wage claim generally must be brought within 2 years of accrual, extended to 3 years if the employer's violation was willful.
facts.sourceAgency: Colorado Dept of Labor & Employment, Division of Labor Standards and Statistics
facts.notes: Colorado Wage Act. Willfulness means intentional or reckless disregard of the law.

facts.value: protected: good-faith health/safety and fraud reports
facts.summary: Colorado's Protected Health/Safety Expression and Whistleblowing (PHEW) Act bars an employer from disciplining, discriminating against, or retaliating against a worker (employee or independent contractor) for raising a reasonable, good-faith concern about a workplace violation of a government health or safety rule, or a significant workplace health/safety threat; a related provision also protects reports of fraud against public benefit programs.
facts.citation: C.R.S. § 8-14.4-101 et seq. (as amended by SB 22-097)
facts.sourceAgency: Colorado Dept of Labor & Employment, Division of Labor Standards and Statistics
facts.notes: cdle.colorado.gov blocks automated fetch (CloudFront 403) for this and other CO facts' sourceUrls; content confirmed via WebSearch result snippets describing CDLE's own INFO #5A guidance and secondary law-firm summaries (Littler, Fisher Phillips) of the 2022 SB 22-097 expansion. Workers may file a complaint with CDLE, which can proceed to state court. Separate from this general health/safety whistleblower law, Colorado also has a State Employee Protection Act (C.R.S. § 24-50.5-101 et seq.) covering only public employees, and Colorado recognizes a common-law wrongful-discharge-in-violation-of-public-policy claim not codified here.

facts.value: discharge: immediately (or within 6/24 hours if payroll unit is closed); resignation: next regular payday
facts.summary: Under the Colorado Wage Act, an employee's earned, unpaid wages are due immediately upon a discharge by the employer (with a short grace period if the accounting unit isn't open), while an employee who resigns is paid on the next regular payday.
facts.sourceAgency: Colorado Dept of Labor & Employment, Division of Labor Standards and Statistics
facts.notes: cdle.colorado.gov blocks automated fetch for this tool (as with other CO facts' sourceUrls); content confirmed via WebSearch result snippets (including the Colorado Office of the State Controller's own summary) describing immediate-on-discharge payment with narrow 6-hour/24-hour extensions when the accounting unit isn't operating, a 10-calendar-day property/equipment audit allowance, and next-payday timing for a voluntary resignation.

facts.summary: An employment discrimination charge with the Colorado Civil Rights Division must be filed within 300 days of the alleged discriminatory act, or it is barred.
facts.notes: CCRD cannot extend this statutory deadline. Intake submission alone does not constitute a filed formal complaint.
